value.body: Some MBBS graduates build careers in research — clinical trials, epidemiology, public-health studies or laboratory science — instead of full-time clinical practice. The main public employer is the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and its institutes; medical colleges, AIIMS-type institutes and other science agencies also run research groups. Most research careers need further study, such as an MD, a PhD or a research fellowship.

items.label: Apex body
items.note: Founded in 1911 as the Indian Research Fund Association; renamed ICMR in 1949

items.label: Student research grant
items.note: For MBBS and BDS students; running since 1979

value.title: How you get in
value.body: An MBBS with registration is the base. Common routes: ICMR scientist recruitment notices, an MD followed by research posts, a PhD (some institutes offer MD-PhD or PhD after MBBS), or research fellowships from government science agencies and charitable funders. Most scientist posts ask for a postgraduate degree or research experience.

value.title: At a glance
items: Research posts are fewer than clinical posts and often begin as fixed-term project positions.
Early-career research income is usually lower than private clinical work, and grant funding can be uncertain.
Publications, a good mentor and a research degree matter more here than NEET-PG rank.
Many doctors combine part-time clinical work with research.
